packages.label: כֶּתֶר וּתְשׁוּבָה — Keter and Repentance
packages.label_en: Keter: The Crown of Silence, Repentance, and Divine Honor
packages.reason: This is the central conceptual cluster of Torah #6, orbiting כֶּתֶר (crown/Keter) as the dominant node with 7 direct bechina connections. The teaching's core argument: the person who flees honor, accepts shame in silence, and makes teshuvah achieves כֶּתֶר — the highest sefirah, which is the same in nature as אֶהֱיֶה (the divine name of future-being/potential), תְּשׁוּבָה (repentance), שְׁתִיקָה (silence), כָּבוֹד אֱלֹהִים (divine honor), the upper point of the Aleph, the Throne above the firmament, and מֹשֶׁה (who is the bechina of דַּעַת). Keter = the state of 'אֲנָא זָמִין לְמֵהֱוֵי' — I am about to come into being — the threshold moment of teshuvah, before one has full existence in the world. The 'כָּ"ף' of כָּבוֹד = כֶּתֶר = הַמְתָּנָה (waiting/patience) = the divine helping hand that meets the person who purifies himself. The cluster includes: the prophetic-Ezekiel vision terminology ('וּמִמַּעַל לָרָקִיעַ דְּמוּת כִּסֵּא וְנַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם לָשֶׁבֶת עַל הַכִּסֵּא' = 'בַּמְּכֻסֶּה מִמְּךָ אַל תַּחְקֹר'), confirming that keter/the throne cannot be investigated — it is the concealed divine honor. Moshe as the upper point = daat = the Temple (כְּאִלּוּ נִבְנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ). Merged into this package: (a) כָּבוֹד אֱלֹהִים ↔ שֶׁמֶן — divine honor = anointing oil (same essential nature as keter-anointing); (b) חֲכָמִים ↔ אַוָּזֵי — the wise are called 'geese' in a dream (the geese-wisdom connection from Rabba bar bar Chana's vision, whose silence made him worthy of this revelation, same nature as keter/silence cluster); (c) יִשְׂרָאֵל ↔ אָדָם — Israel = Adam, the human who sits on the throne (the אָדָם עַל הַכִּסֵּא is the central image of the throne-vision = keter); (d) בָּקִי ↔ שֵׁם יב"ק — 'expert' = the divine name Yabak (connecting the expertise in ratzo-vshuv to the overall teshuvah path); (e) דֶּרֶךְ ↔ שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים הַשֵּׁם יב"ק — the Way of teshuvah = twice the name Yabak gematria (the outcome of possessing both bechina-expertise = the road of teshuvah itself); (f) כְּבוֹד עוֹלָם הַבָּא ↔ תְּשׁוּבָה שְׁנִיָּה and תְּשׁוּבָה עַל תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ — the second teshuvah (repenting on one's first teshuvah upon reaching higher perception) = World-to-Come honor = this is the upper dimension of teshuvah = keter nature.
nodes: "וממעל לרקיע דמות כסא וכו, ונעשה אדם לשבת על הכסא"
"וממעל לרקיע אשר על ראשם אבן ספיר דמות כסא"
merge_notes: Component (כבוד אלהים, שמן): Divine honor equated to anointing oil (שמן) — through silence one merits divine honor which is in its essential nature the anointing of the king (Psalm 45: 'you loved righteousness, therefore God anointed you'). This is the same nature as כתר (crown/anointing). Merged by shared nature: divine-honor-as-anointing = keter.

Component (חכמים, אוזי): The wise men (חכמים) that Rabba bar bar Chana saw are equated with geese (אוזי) — from the Talmud (Berakhot 57b): one who sees a goose in a dream should expect wisdom. This is part of the Rabba bar bar Chana parable about humility (treading like a desert), which is the same virtue cluster as silence/keter. The goose-wisdom identity is a bechina of the silent humility that produces wisdom. Merged by shared nature: wisdom from humility = keter-wisdom cluster.

Component (ישראל, אדם): Israel = Adam (the human being). In the context of Torah 6, this is the 'אדם על הכסא' (human sitting on the throne) — the central image of the Ezekiel throne-vision. Israel being the אדם connects directly to the Keter/throne/upper-point cluster, since the throne-vision is the primary metaphor for keter in this Torah. Merged by shared nature: Israel as the throne-occupant = keter cluster.

Component (בקי, שם יב"ק): 'Expert' (בקי) = the divine name Yabak (יב"ק) — because the letters of Yabak spell Baki. Yabak is the combined divine name used in teshuvah prayer; achieving baki in both ratzo and shuv produces the Way (דרך) of teshuvah. This is the synthesis-achievement that belongs to the teshuvah/keter package as the crowning attainment. Merged by shared nature: expert-in-teshuvah = the way of keter.

Component (דרך, שתי פעמים השם יב"ק): The 'Way' (דרך, numerically = 2 × Yabak) is the way of teshuvah itself — the outcome of having both bechina-expertises (ratzo and shuv). This is thematically the culmination of the whole teaching, landing in the 'Way of teshuvah' which = keter = the crown achievement. Merged by shared nature: the Way of teshuvah = keter.

Component (כבוד עולם הבא, תשובה שניה, תשובה על תשובתו): The second teshuvah is teshuvah done on the first teshuvah — when one reaches greater divine perception, the previous level seems insufficient and one repents on it. This second/higher teshuvah is in its essential nature 'כבוד עולם הבא' (World-to-Come honor), equated in the text with 'כבוד אלקים הסתר דבר' — the concealed divine honor = keter. Three-node component merged into Package 1 by shared nature: upper-teshuvah = keter.

packages.label: נְקֻדָּה תַּחְתּוֹנָה — The Lower Point: Yehoshua, Moon, and Earth
packages.label_en: The Lower Dot of the Aleph: Yehoshua, the Moon, and the Earthly Domain
packages.reason: This cluster is the lower structural pole of the Aleph (אָלֶ"ף), which is the Torah's master metaphor for the triune structure of reality (upper point / vav / lower point = heaven / firmament / earth = Moshe / ohel / Yehoshua). The lower dot of the Aleph = יְהוֹשֻׁעַ = לְבָנָה (the moon) = 'וְהָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי' (the earth as God's footstool) = נְקֻדַּת חִירִיק (the vowel-point for the lowest level). Yehoshua is the lower aspect because 'the destruction of Amalek's seed depends on Yehoshua' — he is the warrior who fights at ground level (נְקֻדָּה תַּחְתּוֹנָה = the aspect that subdues the nations beneath). The moon/levana is this point because it receives light from above (Moshe/sun = upper point) and rules the night-domain. Merged into this package: (a) דְּמִימָה ↔ 'הֲדֹם' ↔ הַנְּקֻדָּה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁל תְּמוּנַת א — silence/stillness is the lower point of the aleph shape; the Hebrew word 'הֲדֹם' (footstool) = דְּמִימָה (silence/stillness) because both describe the receptive-passive lower dimension; (b) תְּשׁוּבָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה ↔ כְּבוֹד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה — the first (lower/initial) teshuvah is by nature the honor of this world — the earthly-level teshuvah corresponds to the lower point; (c) יְכַלּוּ זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק ↔ 'יַדְבֵּר עַמִּים תַּחְתֵּינוּ' — Amalek's defeat = 'He subdues peoples beneath us' (Psalm 47) = the lower-point subduing the earthly enemies = same nature as Yehoshua/lower-point.
merge_notes: Component ('הדם', דמימה, הנקדה התחתונה של תמונת א): The word 'הֲדֹם' (footstool) = דְּמִימָה (silence/stillness/arrest). Both are the essential nature of the lower point of the Aleph shape. דְּמִימָה literally means becoming still — the earth as God's footstool is the image of total stillness/receptivity beneath the divine. The lower point of the aleph-shape is this very stillness-point. Merged by shared nature: the footstool-stillness = lower point.

Component (תשובה הראשונה, כבוד עולם הזה): The first (lower-level) teshuvah is in its essential nature the honor of this world. The Torah teaches a two-tier teshuvah: first is earthly-level teshuvah (honoring the Earthly domain), second is the concealed/divine teshuvah (= keter, Package 1). The first tier's essential nature aligns with the lower point (earthly, 'הֲדֹם') domain. Merged by shared nature: first/earthly teshuvah = lower-point domain.

Component (יכלו זרעו של עמלק, 'ידבר עמים תחתינו'): The annihilation of Amalek's seed is equated with 'He subdues peoples beneath us' (Psalm 47:4) = the lower point (תַּחְתֵּינוּ = beneath us). Amalek's defeat is the lower-point's defining action — Yehoshua fights Amalek at the ground level. While node_id 'יכלו זרעו של עמלק' is distinct from 'להכרית זרעו של עמלק', both refer to the same theme and the former's bechina-partner 'ידבר עמים תחתינו' explicitly describes the lower-point domain. Merged by shared nature: lower-point subduing = lower-point cluster.

packages.label: הַוָּא"ו שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הָאָלֶ"ף — The Vav: Firmament, Shame, and Gaon Yaakov
packages.label_en: The Middle Vav of the Aleph: Firmament, the Blush of Shame, and Royal Gaon
packages.reason: The middle element of the Aleph (the vav/וָּא"ו connecting upper and lower dots) = the רָקִיעַ (firmament) = the mediating space of fire and water = the phenomenon of בּוּשָׁה (blushing shame), because the firmament changes colors just as a face that blushes changes from red to white. The vav is also the אֹהֶל (tent = Moshe's tent of meeting = the space where upper and lower meet). 'לְמַנּוֹת לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ' = appointing a king = the nature of the firmament/vav, because the king is the mediating royal presence between heaven and earth. 'גְּאוֹן יַעֲקֹב' = the pride/greatness of Jacob = the nature of the appointed king = 'דָּרַךְ כּוֹכָב מִיַּעֲקֹב' (a star shall stride from Jacob) = the kingly comet/star that traverses from Yaakov = מֶלֶךְ. This cluster captures the mediating royal-shame dimension: shame is the emotion of standing between two poles (red/white, honored/shamed, heaven/earth) — the exact position of the vav/firmament.

packages.label: בָּקִי בְּרָצוֹא — Expert in Ascending
packages.label_en: Bakhi b'Ratzo: The Upward Motion — Never Standing Still on a High Level
packages.reason: This cluster captures the first of two spiritual expertise-dimensions taught in Torah #6. 'בָּקִי בְּרָצוֹא' (expert in the outward rush) = the person who reaches a high spiritual level and does NOT rest there but continues to ascend higher — 'אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֵינוֹ עוֹמֵד שָׁם, וְהוּא מִתְחַזֵּק וּמִתְגַּבֵּר לַעֲלוֹת יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר' (even so he does not stay there, but strengthens himself to go higher and higher). This is equated with: 'עַיִל' (the entering/ascending motion), 'אֲנִי לְדוֹדִי' (I am for my beloved — the worshipper moving toward God), 'אִם אֶסַּק שָׁמַיִם שָׁם אָתָּה' (if I ascend to heaven, You are there), and 'סֶגּוֹל דְּקס"א' (the vowel-segol of the divine name Ehyeh=161, because 'אֶסַּק' has the same letters as 'קס"א'). This is the ascending pole of the Ratzo-veShov (running and returning) dynamic from Ezekiel's vision — the 'חַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב' that the Torah uses as its structural metaphor for spiritual persistence. Together with Package 5 (Bakhi b'Shuv), this forms the two-dimensional expertise of the person on the path of teshuvah.
nodes: הינו בין שיזכה לאיזו עליה, לאיזו מדרגה גדולה, אף על פי כן אל יעמד שם, ולא יסתפק עצמו בזה, רק צריך שיהיה בקי בזה מאד, לידע ולהאמין שהוא צריך ללכת יותר ויותר וכו

packages.label: בָּקִי בְּשׁוֹב — Expert in Descending
packages.label_en: Bakhi b'Shuv: The Downward Motion — Never Despairing Even in the Lowest Place
packages.reason: This cluster captures the second of two spiritual expertise-dimensions: 'בָּקִי בְּשׁוֹב' (expert in the inward/downward return) = the person who falls to a very low spiritual level and does NOT despair — 'שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ אִם יִפֹּל לִמְקוֹם שֶׁיִּפֹּל אֲפִלּוּ בִּשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיּוֹת, גַּם כֵּן אַל יִתְיָאֵשׁ עַצְמוֹ לְעוֹלָם' (even if he falls to the lowest pit of the underworld, he must never despair). This is equated with: 'נָפִיק' (the exiting/descending motion), 'וְדוֹדִי לִי' (and my beloved is for me — God reaching down even to the fallen), 'וְאַצִּיעָה שְׁאוֹל הִנֶּךָּ' (if I make my bed in the underworld, You are there — Psalm 139), and 'חִירִיק דְס"ג' (the vowel-chirik of the divine name Havayah=63, associated with the lowest level where God's presence still lives). This corresponds to the 'shoov' (returning) half of the Ratzo-veShov dynamic. The teaching is radical: expertise in falling without despairing is as important as expertise in rising. Together with Package 4, these two form the complete two-bechina teshuvah skill that produces the Way (דֶּרֶךְ = Package 1 merged).
nodes: שאפלו אם יפל, חס ושלום, למקום שיפל אפלו בשאול תחתיות, גם כן אל יתיאש עצמו לעולם, ותמיד יחפש ויבקש את השם יתברך, ויחזק עצמו בכל מקום שהוא, בכל מה שיוכל, כי גם בשאול תחתיות נמצא השם יתברך, וגם שם יכולין לדבק את עצמו אליו יתברך

packages.label: בִּזְיוֹנוֹת וּמַחֲלֹקֶת — Shame, Strife, and the Evil Inclination
packages.label_en: The Evil Mirror: Seeking Honor Produces Strife and the Withdrawal of God's Face
packages.reason: This is the evil counterpart of the positive keter-teshuvah teaching. Torah #6 opens with the antithesis: the person who PURSUES honor (in contrast to the one who flees it) loses divine honor and gains instead 'כְּבוֹד מְלָכִים' — human/royal honor that is constantly challenged and scrutinized ('כְּבֹד מְלָכִים חֲקֹר דָּבָר'). The evil side of the teaching is expressed through two bechina-pairs: (1) נוֹצוֹת (feathers from the goose/wisdom bird) = מַחֲלֹקֶת וּבִזְיוֹנוֹת (strife and shaming) — the feathers plucked from the wisdom-goose represent the honor-seeker who plucks honor from wisdom without achieving it, producing only conflict; (2) בִּזְיוֹנוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים (shaming and bloodshed) = הַסְתָּרַת וְהַחְזָרַת פְּנֵי אקי"ה (the concealing and revealing of the divine face of Ehyeh). The evil person who has abundant blood in the left chamber of the heart (the dwelling of the evil inclination) brings upon himself shaming and bloodshed — which is the divine face turning away and back. This is the structural opposite of Package 1: instead of silence-humility-teshuvah producing keter (divine honor concealed), honor-seeking produces public shaming and divine withdrawal. The two evil-domain components are merged by shared nature: both describe the consequences of ego-driven honor-pursuit = the antithesis of keter.
merge_notes: Component (נוצות, מחלקת ובזיונות): Goose-feathers = strife and shaming. The goose in Torah 6 is the wisdom-bird (חֲכָמִים = אַוָּזֵי, in Package 1). The feathers being plucked = the wisdom being stripped from its source by honor-seekers, leaving only strife. Evil mirror of the חכמים/אוזי node in Package 1. Merged into this evil package by shared nature: the evil consequence of honor-pursuit.

Component (בזיונות ושפיכות דמים, הסתרת והחזרת פני אקי"ה): The shaming and bloodshed experienced by the person with excess left-chamber blood (= evil inclination still strong) is in its essential nature the divine face (אקי"ה = Ehyeh = keter-name) turning away and returning. This is the evil mirror of the keter-teshuvah teaching: instead of the keter-light descending, it hides. Merged into this evil package by shared nature: withdrawal of the divine keter-presence as consequence of evil inclination.
